Automod for Stoat servers
Stoat Automod: Configurable Moderation for Stoat Servers
Configure Stoatmod automod categories, thresholds, review modes and moderator safeguards for a Stoat server.
Stoat automod
Choose what Stoatmod watches, how confident a match must be and what the bot should do when a configured category crosses that threshold.
Automatic does not mean uncontrolled

Stoatmod checks text and qualifying images against the moderation categories a server enables. A category only triggers when its score is greater than the effective threshold and its configured action permits an intervention.

Policy Studio separates observation from enforcement. Teams can watch matches first, move selected categories into review and enable stronger actions only after they understand the effect on their own community.

Thresholds and category policy

The default moderation threshold is 90%. The dashboard limits normal policy thresholds to 50–100%. The legacy command permits lower values only after a separate confirmation because low thresholds can act on weak background scores.
Show the current threshold.
Set a 90% threshold.
Review enabled moderation categories.
A lower score does not automatically mean a safer or more effective policy. Test changes with real examples and review false positives before enforcing them.
Safety and failure behaviour
Moderation-provider or network failures are fail-open, so the message remains rather than being silently removed.
Suicidal thoughts use an always-enabled supportive DM category without deleting or warning. Promoting self-harm is a separate moderation category.
Moderator exemption is enabled by default and can be changed by the server team.
Cases and event history provide review context, but not every operational event becomes a moderation case.

Spam and mass-mention protection guide
Stoat Spam Protection and Mass-Mention Controls | Stoatmod
Detect rapid messages, repeats, mass mentions and other spam patterns with per-server Stoatmod controls.
Stoat anti-spam bot
Stoatmod combines repeat, speed, mention and message-pattern signals. Each server can tune when those signals trigger and how long the automatic timeout lasts.
What the spam system watches
Exact repeated messages and near-duplicates.
Rapid bursts and a decaying activity score.
Multiple links and character flooding.
A configurable number of unique user and role mentions in one message, plus @everyone or @online.

Spam detection is enabled by default. The starting rules trigger on three identical messages within 30 seconds, five messages within 10 seconds, a behaviour score of five points, or five combined user and role mentions. The behaviour score has a 30-second half-life, and the default timeout is 60 minutes.
Adjust protection for one server
Open the server dashboard, choose Protection Centre, then go to Spam protection. Changes apply only to that server after you select Save all changes; every other server keeps its own settings.
Repeated-message count and window: choose the number of identical consecutive messages and the time in which they must arrive.
Rapid-message count and window: choose the total number of messages and the shorter burst period that triggers the rule.
Trigger score and score memory: set the score needed to trigger and how many seconds of inactivity it takes the score to halve.
Mention limit and timeout length: set the combined user-and-role mention limit and the timeout applied after any spam rule triggers.
Restore defaults: return every spam adjustment to the server defaults before saving.

Higher message counts and shorter windows are more tolerant. A lower trigger score or longer score memory catches suspicious patterns sooner. @everyone and @online always count as mass mentions while spam protection is active.
What enforcement does

Rapid, repeated and scored spam normally produces a timeout and warning, which can also advance the server's warning policy. The triggering message is not always deleted. The mass-mention path separately attempts to delete the message before applying its moderation response.
A timeout does not always remove the triggering message. Check the event details and the bot’s permissions when reviewing an incident.

A policy filter, not a reputation scanner
Link protection recognises common HTTP, HTTPS and FTP URLs, www links, valid bare domains and IP-address links. When enabled, it attempts to remove matching messages.
This filter blocks external links according to your rules. It does not check whether the destination is safe or malicious.
Behaviour and exceptions
Link protection is disabled by default.
A routine link removal does not add a warning.
The dashboard can allow gifbox.me and its subdomains.

How image scanning works

Image scanning is experimental, may not be accurate, and is off by default. When a server owner enables it, qualifying uploads are checked only for severe graphic real-world violence and explicit sexual content. Ordinary image attachments over 10 MiB are skipped.

New-account and join protection
Protect a Stoat Server from Suspicious New Accounts | Stoatmod
Use Stoatmod verification, account-age checks and controlled bypasses for suspicious new accounts joining a Stoat server.
Stoat join protection
Give suspicious new accounts a private verification path before they can fully participate, with clear expiry and moderator recovery controls.
Default eligibility

Join protection is off by default. Server moderators can enable a browser CAPTCHA for accounts younger than 14 days. A separate dashboard option can require verification for everyone and is disabled by default. Accounts younger than seven days are highlighted in logs.
A private verification link is sent first.
A one-day timeout is applied when the challenge is created.
The member has 30 minutes to complete the check.
Three failed checks or expiry can lead to a kick.
Important delivery and rollback behaviour

If Stoatmod cannot deliver the private message, it does not apply the timeout or challenge. If setup fails after a timeout is applied, it attempts to roll the member back and records whether moderator action is still needed.
Disabling join protection can still leave existing challenged members restricted when Timeout Members permission is missing. Check both the setting and the real member state.

Moderation cases and review history
Stoat Moderation Cases, Warnings and Review History | Stoatmod
Record warnings and eligible moderation actions as reviewable Stoatmod cases with reasons, evidence and appeal status.
Accountable moderation
Bring the action, reason and follow-up into one server-scoped record. Find a member’s history, add context and give your team a clear starting point for review.
What belongs in a case
Warnings and manual mutes.
Spam or policy timeouts and bans.
Stoatmod-initiated kicks and manual bans.
Appeals, moderator notes and supported evidence attachments.

Warnings and eligible moderation actions can create a case, with notes and appeals connected to the record. Routine link deletions and general operational events may appear only in event history. Actions taken outside Stoatmod may not identify the acting moderator.
Make the reason part of the action

Moderation commands require a reason. For mutes, put the duration before or after the reason; leaving it out uses one hour. The examples below use a placeholder USER_ID—replace it with a member’s ID or mention.
Add a warning with a reason.
Mute for 25 minutes. You can also write the reason before 25m.
Remove a timeout and record the reason.
Unban a member and record the reason for reversal.
Removing a case with ~remove CASE_ID is the exception: it does not require a reason. Case removal and reversing a punishment are separate actions.
Warning and removal behaviour

The default warning ladder acts at three, five and seven active warnings: timeout, kick and ban. A server can replace this with staged dashboard policy. Removing a warning case stops it counting while retaining the case as removed. Removing a non-warning case does not undo its punishment.
